# Polling and timed-wait inventory

Baseline: `d33ed17571`. Locations refer to that baseline so deletion does not erase the audit trail. A location explicitly followed by a revision names a later source composition at that revision.

Scope: `rust/crates/**` and `typescript/packages/**`, excluding the separately owned `harness`, `harness-core`, `harness-tui` and `harness-client` packages. Product code, tests, conformance, examples, benchmarks and scripts are included. Exact publicly released Harness caller slices are composed atomically with their primitive contracts; their sites are explicitly recorded below.

The expanded test scope also includes tests in those packages and every test
harness. Its full current-source census is pending. Ordinary test readiness
uses the producer's event. Deliberately defective polling negative controls and
workload holds retain their independent oracle and exact classification; they
do not authorize a test-folder or helper exemption. A registry without an
observable publication event returns unobservable instead of probing again.

Candidates include event-driven loops and retry identity references; these require classification, not mechanical removal. Pending rows are not approval to retain a timer. The only timing exceptions are caller-chosen request deadlines and backoff following transient transport failure. Tool/model retry and exact idempotent resend identities are allowed. Actor alarm implementations are the event primitive itself.

## Producer and terminal priorities

| Consumer | Original producer and completion | Outstanding terminal or disposition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native mount mutation qualification | Actual mounted I/O child writes the sentinel; native watcher delivers the same mount change | NFS uses a 100 ms directory scanner. An original native mutation event and retained producer-loss terminal are still required; blocking on a retained callback sender would not close the gap. |
| Terminal qualification | Original ConPTY child publishes input, negotiation, wheel and restoration files; physical output reader owns stdout EOF | Replace file/status samples with the original notification/report and child-exit join. Windows cancellation still needs the original submitted-read acknowledgement and physical completion. |
| Workload authority | Real issuing root and its retained verifier share the supplied trusted clock | Signed expiry conformance uses the same clock and a successful preparation before advancing it. Device providers without push must return truthful Pending; workload time is not an operation-deadline wake event. |
| Backend startup and child generation | Original server endpoint stdout, service pipe header/EOF, native child completion and HTTP child generation | Endpoint and service waits use original producer events. The backend child-generation gate still retains its own sender; runtime admission/refusal must supply its terminal before removing the timer. Disposable database/object server scripts still lack final-start event ownership. |
| Registry visibility | Original npm/cargo publisher child exits; each explicit registry query has one response | Registry propagation has no push subscription here. Return typed Unobservable after one observation, with exact caller resume identity; never hide propagation behind a timed probe window. |
| Compiler and file barriers | Original compiler subprocess exit, actual generated artifact admission, native watch batch/fence and provider release event | Keep exact artifact/source checks after compiler exit. Do not poll for output files or retry a lost fence. Cross-source static helper coverage and unreviewed script candidates remain open. |
| Release publication | Each original tag-object read, asset upload and release edit returns its own result | Preserve immutable source/digest resend checks. Traverse actual tag ancestry without an arbitrary nesting bound; no periodic release or asset visibility query. |

## Logical capacity audit

Audit basis: design audit v3 (2026-10-30), axis (f), and gap register G63Ã¢â‚¬â€œG67. This inventory distinguishes limits on complete logical work from pages, scheduling credit, physical protocol constraints and explicit caller capacity. Status starts as **open**; completion requires removal of the refusal/truncation and its hidden default, with consumer updates.

Excluded: `harness`, `harness-core`, `harness-tui`, `harness-client`, and `typescript/packages/harness` (tracked separately in #1744). MCP startup/tool defaults, agent depth/goals/checkpoints/children/history and the shell preset in those packages remain in that scope. The filesystem shell adapter must preserve the optional caller deadline supplied by that work.

## Native batch arrival

`NativeWatch::wait_for_changes_with_native_work` observes the original retained queue and native-batch boundary on the watch's existing condition variable. It does not consume hints or write a fence cookie. Inotify brackets the same serialized drain, so an arrival observer cannot seal a half-delivered rename. Its original delivery sink also receives permanent producer loss; both physical retirement paths publish that terminal before withdrawing their original owner. A rescan can clear ordinary continuity loss, but cannot resurrect a physically retired producer. Native source callback reentry and partial startup return their retained typed failure.

Safety controls use real file writes and a rename, with a physically settled early batch as the event-before-subscribe negative control. Cancellation and physical inotify retirement race the original arrival registration without a timer. Progress has one producer: completion of that original native batch, or its retained loss/cancellation terminal. The Linux named control also asserts that waiting adds zero backend reads and writes. The native library compiled on Linux x86_64 with `cargo check --locked -p acyclic-fs --lib` (39.30 s compiler time); the named real write/rename, retained-early-event, cancellation and physical-retirement control passed at `75754ebba1` (1/1, 0.00 s). macOS and consumer execution remain unqualified.

Required per-operation work: the existing queue and condition remain one each, with no added worker, task, queue, scan, durability barrier, round trip or payload copy. A cancellable blocked observer retains the existing O(1) cancellation registration and notification allocation. The two inotify batch-boundary locks are fixed work per native drain, independent of queued history; no idle native event means no condition notification. Remaining consumer polling rows stay pending until they use this event.

## Rejecting source rule

Pending: `scripts/check-no-polling.mjs <baseline-revision>` compares real Git objects with tracked and untracked sources in the working tree. `scripts/no-polling.mjs` rejects new timer/readiness references, aliases, embedded timer programs and unclassified loops. JavaScript/TypeScript uses an explicitly declared compiler-API parser dependency; native sources retain raw-string and nested-comment boundaries. Each disposition names one exact source fingerprint, classification, producer, terminal and negative control. Changing executable tokens reopens dispositions in that source unit; an accepted occurrence cannot authorize another copy.

The source controls cover direct timers, imported and assigned aliases, wrapped timer values, computed property concatenation, dynamic calls, template substitutions, regex boundaries, escaped identifiers, rechecks, child-status probes and timed condition waits. JavaScript/TypeScript dependency controls additionally cover renamed/namespace/default imports, re-exports, escaped object methods, lexical shadowing, recursive helper groups, changed helpers with unchanged callers, module side effects and lost local source. Dependencies identify declarations, not shared function spellings. An exact disposition for a helper does not authorize a new caller. Unresolved relative/workspace imports remain candidates for review rather than being silently exempted.

Both snapshots reuse one parsed AST per script source. Native token streams are released after recording their sites. The dependency graph is finite source analysis; it has no timer, periodic task, generated code or per-reference I/O. Graph traversal visits each edge a fixed number of times; canonical fingerprint ordering additionally sorts component members and outgoing digests. No constant-time claim is made for the complete source analysis. Git subprocesses increase from three to four: one baseline tree enumeration preserves deleted producers, with all original blobs still read through one batch. Controls use actual Git objects, including staged producer deletion and untracked consumers.

All 13 source controls passed on Linux x86_64 with `node --test scripts/no-polling.test.mjs` (2.10 s), after declaring the parser dependency and generating the lockfile with the actual package manager. Required-check integration, exact disposition review, native cross-file bindings, dynamic initialization and external export resolution remain pending; this source checkpoint does not close the static-rule obligation. Run the contributor command after installing dependencies: `bun run check:no-polling origin/main`.

The local durable-root reopening control also consumes `OwnershipReleaseBarrier::released()` directly before reacquiring the original provider locks. This replaces the later-added ten-second deadline and blocking-wait task at `filesystem/src/tests/facade/local.rs`; no timer or worker is needed to observe final provider destruction.

The crash-left fence contention control also deletes its later-added five-second output wait and 16 KiB retained-output ceiling. Original stdout is consumed once into a sink after readiness; physical exit remains owned by `ProcessTree`. Readiness and release use two pipes per child, with no temporary files, status probes, extra reader thread, payload retention or product resource. The lost-release negative control adds one actual child invocation; the original two contenders remain.


## Explicit registry publication terminals

Registry propagation has no push subscription in the current Cargo/npm commands. An accepted publisher exit therefore leads to one observation, then either exact verified visibility or `RegistryPublicationPending` (`REGISTRY_PUBLICATION_PENDING`). Pending retains the observed archive/tag and original publisher status, and stops dependent publication. It carries the exact caller command; the caller chooses any later resend. Different archives and yanked versions retain refusal. Neither command sleeps or probes until visible.

Required work per selected publication, counted from source:

| Boundary | Before | Current source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| npm archive already visible | Preflight integrity plus repeated integrity/latest pairs, five-second pauses and a five-minute window | Reuse the preflight integrity and read latest once: three queries on immediate success become two; no timer, clock read, task or periodic query |
| npm newly accepted archive | One original publish child, then repeated integrity/latest queries | Same one publish child, at most one integrity and one latest observation; absent visibility terminates Pending before any dependent archive |
| Cargo newly accepted archive | One original publish child, then up to ninety version observations and two-second pauses | Same one publish child, one observation; absent visibility terminates Pending |
| Cargo publication race | One reconciliation read, then another visibility read | One original post-terminal observation serves reconciliation and visibility together |
| Caller recovery text | No typed Pending command | Formatting and one Error/observation record only on the failure path; verified publication adds no command array/string allocation or extra process |
| Annotated release tag | One API read per tag, but a depth counter refused after eleven ancestors | Same one read per actual immutable ancestor; no counter or total cap; exact source/object checks remain |

One original compiler/publisher exit and each actual registry response own progress. No background producer is invented for index propagation. Payload hashing/packaging, metadata enumeration and actual tag ancestry remain proportional to requested input; the selected-version response replaces the registry version-history scan, publication output ceilings are removed, and release assets are indexed once. Decoding the actual metadata and hashing selected artifacts remain proportional to their input. No new syscall, durability barrier, round trip or payload copy is added on verified paths. The new real Node/shell control exercises exact original flags/quoted arguments and a naive-quote negative; the real Git control uses fourteen actual annotated tags and a later HEAD. Their output comes from those binaries, with no fabricated external-tool or registry fixture. Source-rule controls restore the removed two/five-second mechanisms. The real Node/shell and Git controls passed on Linux x86_64 at f56588ca65 (2/2, 0.194 s execution, 83.0 s total). The source-rule restoration controls remain unrun; Windows/macOS execution is not claimed.

## Selected publication metadata and output ownership

The registry provider's [original version metadata controller](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io/blob/main/src/controllers/version/metadata.rs)
defines the selected-version route and its single `version` response field.
Cargo publication uses that route once, then admits the original version,
checksum and yanked state. It no longer downloads every version of the crate.
Response decoding still costs the bytes actually returned by that provider;
this does not claim constant-size provider records or live publication proof.

Release asset lookup builds one Map from the original response. For N returned
assets and K requested artifacts, repeated lookup work changes from O(N*K) to
O(N+K), paying one Map and N entries once. Actual enumeration, payload hashing
and required publication calls remain proportional to selected work. Original
immutable source, digest and exact resend checks are unchanged.

Cargo, npm and release commands explicitly capture unbounded original output.
The two fixed ceilings and npm's implicit adapter ceiling are removed. No new
child, timer, query, durability barrier or payload copy is added. This source
change has not executed a publication and adds no fabricated provider fixture.
